title: Determinants and unstable cores in sequential distributive phosphorylation
abstract: Vassena and Stadler (arXiv:2308.11486v3, Supplementary Example D) conjectured that sequential distributive phosphorylation cycles have only unstable-positive cores and that every invertible child-selection matrix has determinant of absolute value one. The determinant assertion is proved, and the restriction to unstable-positive cores is disproved. In the n-site cycle, every child-selection matrix has determinant 0, 1 or -1. For every n >= 3, a six-species child-selection matrix is minimally Hurwitz-unstable and has determinant 1, giving an unstable-negative core. For every n >= 2, there is an unstable-positive core on 2n+1 species, so their sizes are unbounded; every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under every positive column scaling. For every n >= 3, there is also a five-species D-unstable core: a positive column scaling makes it unstable, while every proper principal submatrix remains nonunstable under all such scalings.
